title: Origin-isolating SRS file discovery with steps directory partition
statement: discoverSrsFiles partitions discovered .srs.md files into body scope files and step files, where step files match /docs/spec/steps/<name>/*.srs.md and body files exclude /docs/rule/ and /docs/spec/steps/, exposing step files via SrsFileSet.stepFiles[] without including them in scopeFiles.
ac: Files under docs/spec/steps/<name>/ ending in .srs.md appear in SrsFileSet.stepFiles[] and never in SrsFileSet.scopeFiles.
Files under docs/rule/ are excluded from both scopeFiles and stepFiles.
A body scope file outside steps/ continues to appear in scopeFiles unchanged.
SrsFileSet.stepFiles is present (possibly empty array) on all returned file sets.

title: Workspace parser origin split into body and step records
statement: The workspace parser flattens body files into records and step files into stepRecords, injecting RequirementRecord.origin ('body'|'step') and stepName, and excludes step files from both workspace.files and workspace.records while exposing stepRecords, stepFiles, and stateFile on ParsedWorkspace.
ac: Requirements parsed from step files carry origin=step and a populated stepName; requirements from body files carry origin=body.
Step requirements appear only in ParsedWorkspace.stepRecords and never in workspace.records or workspace.files.
ParsedWorkspace exposes stepRecords, stepFiles, and stateFile fields.
Consumers reading the new fields default missing values so existing fixtures parse without modification.
depends_on_titles: Origin-isolating SRS file discovery with steps directory partition

title: Optional origin and stepName fields on RequirementRecord and ParsedWorkspace types
statement: types.ts adds optional origin ('body'|'step') and stepName to RequirementRecord and optional stepRecords, stepFiles, and stateFile to ParsedWorkspace so that new fields are backward compatible with existing single-constructor and fixture call sites.
ac: RequirementRecord declares optional origin and stepName fields.
ParsedWorkspace declares optional stepRecords, stepFiles, and stateFile fields.
Existing code constructing RequirementRecord or ParsedWorkspace without the new fields type-checks unchanged.

title: E012 id resolution over union of body and step records
statement: The SRS-E012 referential-existence rule resolves trace references against the union of body records and step records (ids = body plus step) while the E002 duplicate-id rule iterates body records only, so cross-origin traces resolve and a step requirement sharing a body id does not trigger E002.
ac: A trace whose reference exists only in a step requirement resolves without E012.
A step requirement sharing an identical id with a body requirement does not emit E002.
W018 and E025 are not emitted for step scope files because discoveredScopeDocuments is files-based and step files are excluded.
HEAD diagnostics are zero when a step file declares the same ID as an unregistered scope.
depends_on_titles: Workspace parser origin split into body and step records

title: Origin-aware record loading for mutation routing
statement: loadRecord and loadRecordWithWorkspace accept optional origin and stepName parameters that, when omitted, prefer body records for backward compatibility, and when provided route the lookup to step records, enabling step mutations dispatched explicitly from MCP/CLI entry points.
ac: loadRecord with no origin returns the body record for an id present in both body and step.
loadRecord with origin=step and a stepName returns the matching step record.
Existing callers that pass no origin/stepName resolve body records identically to current behavior.
depends_on_titles: Workspace parser origin split into body and step records
Optional origin and stepName fields on RequirementRecord and ParsedWorkspace types

title: Successor trace search over union records to prevent slot regression
statement: findIncomingTraceRows receives the union of body and step records so that successor-slot derivation in update-status and update-stability continues to resolve incoming supersedes traces across origins without regression.
ac: findIncomingTraceRows resolves an incoming supersedes trace whose source is a step record when given the union of records.
deriveSuccessorSlot in update-status produces the same successor heading slot for body-only inputs as before this change.
update-stability successor handling resolves incoming traces over the union input.
depends_on_titles: Origin-aware record loading for mutation routing

title: updateStatus verified-regression exit guard with explicit override
statement: updateStatus denies a transition to discarded with MUTATION_DENIED when the current status is verified, or stability is frozen or stable, or status is implemented with verification evidence, unless an explicit override is supplied via reason plus confirmDiscardVerified.
ac: Transitioning a verified requirement to discarded without confirmDiscardVerified returns MUTATION_DENIED.
Transitioning a frozen or stable requirement to discarded without confirmDiscardVerified returns MUTATION_DENIED.
Transitioning an implemented requirement that has verification evidence to discarded without confirmDiscardVerified returns MUTATION_DENIED.
Supplying reason and confirmDiscardVerified=true allows the discard transition to proceed.
A failing test reproducing the denied transition is written before the guard implementation.

title: state.md loader and parseStepState parser
statement: discover loads docs/spec/steps/state.md via the appendix access-then-read pattern into ParsedWorkspace.stateFile, and parseStepState parses its table (columns Step, Status, DependsOn, TouchesScope, TouchesReq, Created, Updated; Status enum active|merging|merged|abandoned; metadata Step Warn Threshold=7 and Stale Days=14) by reusing parseMarkdownTable.
ac: When docs/spec/steps/state.md exists it is loaded and exposed as ParsedWorkspace.stateFile.
parseStepState returns one entry per state.md row with all seven columns populated.
parseStepState flags a Status value outside active, merging, merged, abandoned.
parseStepState reuses parseMarkdownTable rather than a new table parser.
Absence of state.md yields an undefined stateFile without error.
depends_on_titles: Origin-isolating SRS file discovery with steps directory partition

title: ValidationRule ctx extension and validateWorkspaceScoped step-local pass
statement: The ValidationRule signature is extended to (workspace, ctx?) and validateWorkspaceScoped runs a single step-local validation pass over a workspace given ctx carrying origin, stepName, and touches, scoping diagnostics to one step.
ac: ValidationRule accepts an optional ctx argument carrying origin, stepName, and touches.
validateWorkspaceScoped runs validation limited to the named step's records.
Existing rules invoked without ctx behave identically to before the signature change.
depends_on_titles: Workspace parser origin split into body and step records

title: Step validators W044 step-shadows-body and W045 step-overload plus STEP namespace
statement: The diagnostic registry registers SRS-W044 (step requirement shadows a body requirement, warning) and SRS-W045 (step overload at threshold >=7, warning) after the existing maximum W040, and defines a separate STEP_* diagnostic namespace (DIRECT_CONFLICT, OVERLAP, CYCLE, STALE, DRIFT, SUPERSEDE_PROTECTED) that is structurally excluded from release gates as advisory-only.
ac: SRS-W044 is emitted as a warning when a step requirement shadows a body requirement id.
SRS-W045 is emitted as a warning when a step's requirement count reaches or exceeds 7.
W044 and W045 are registered after W040 and do not collide with W041, W042, or W043.
STEP_* diagnostics live in a namespace separate from SRS-E/W codes and never cause a release gate to fail.
depends_on_titles: ValidationRule ctx extension and validateWorkspaceScoped step-local pass

title: MCP validate_step tool registration
statement: An MCP validate_step tool is registered that runs validateWorkspaceScoped for a named step and returns its step-local diagnostics including W044, W045, and STEP_* advisories.
ac: validate_step accepts a step name and returns diagnostics scoped to that step.
validate_step surfaces W044 and W045 warnings when present.
validate_step returns STEP_* diagnostics as advisory and never as gate-failing errors.
depends_on_titles: ValidationRule ctx extension and validateWorkspaceScoped step-local pass

title: speckiwi step validate command
statement: The CLI exposes speckiwi step validate <name> which runs validateWorkspaceScoped for the named step and prints its step-local diagnostics with an exit code reflecting step-local errors only.
ac: speckiwi step validate <name> runs step-local validation for the named step.
The command prints W044, W045, and STEP_* diagnostics for that step.
The command's exit code reflects step-local errors and is not affected by body-scope diagnostics.
depends_on_titles: ValidationRule ctx extension and validateWorkspaceScoped step-local pass

title: computeSemanticSha content-hash utility with fpv1 frozen vector
statement: computeSemanticSha is a pure function exported under the fpv=1 contract that hashes sha1 over fpv1 joined with normalized requirement text, AC text excluding checked state, status, stability, and metadata (DENY={Status,Stability}, Scope included), excluding Trace Links, Verification Evidence, and Change Notes, using norm = CRLF to LF, per-line trailing-whitespace strip, whitespace runs collapsed to one space, and outer trim.
ac: computeSemanticSha excludes the Trace Links, Verification Evidence, and Change Notes sections from the hash input.
computeSemanticSha excludes Status and Stability metadata keys while including Scope metadata.
AC checked/unchecked state does not change the computed hash; AC text does.
Normalization applies CRLF to LF, per-line trailing-whitespace strip, whitespace-run collapse, and outer trim before hashing.
A frozen fpv1 test vector produces the documented hash asserted by an automated test.

title: compareReqId raw-byte ordering and computeBlastRadius closure utility
statement: compareReqId orders two REQ-IDs by raw byte comparison to select the min-side block for single-row normalization, and computeBlastRadius is a pure exported function returning the transitive depends_on closure limited to 2 hops with frozen/stable edges cut.
ac: compareReqId returns a stable ordering based on raw byte comparison of the two REQ-IDs.
computeBlastRadius returns the transitive depends_on closure bounded to at most 2 hops from the seed set.
computeBlastRadius stops traversal at requirements whose stability is frozen or stable.
computeBlastRadius is exported as a pure function with no I/O side effects.

title: parseCompatibilityNotes strict tokenizer for compatibility Notes
statement: parseCompatibilityNotes tokenizes a compatibility-check Notes cell with item separator semicolon-space, keys matching lowercase-and-hyphen, values matching a restricted charset (ellipsis disallowed), recognizing fpv, self, peer, and checked-at, performing charset validation that table-cell.ts (which only rejects pipe/CR/LF) does not.
ac: parseCompatibilityNotes splits items on semicolon-space and parses each into a key/value pair.
Keys or values outside the allowed charset are rejected.
A value containing an ellipsis or other out-of-charset character is rejected.
fpv, self, peer, and checked-at tokens are recognized and surfaced as structured fields.

title: add_compatibility_check mutation with dedup frozen liveness guards and bidirectional pins
statement: add_compatibility_check inserts a single checked_compatible Trace Links row on the min-side REQ-ID block, automatically computing self and peer semanticSha pins and checked-at, guarded by dedup (one row per min-max pair), frozen-block protection, and endpoint liveness (both endpoints exist, status not discarded, stability not deprecated).
ac: add_compatibility_check writes exactly one checked_compatible row on the compareReqId-minimum block with self and peer pins set to current semanticSha values.
A second add_compatibility_check for the same min-max pair is rejected by the dedup guard.
add_compatibility_check on a frozen block is rejected.
add_compatibility_check is rejected when either endpoint is discarded, deprecated, or non-existent.
The written Reference is a bare live REQ-ID that passes SRS-E012 and addTraceLink guards.
depends_on_titles: computeSemanticSha content-hash utility with fpv1 frozen vector
compareReqId raw-byte ordering and computeBlastRadius closure utility
parseCompatibilityNotes strict tokenizer for compatibility Notes

title: refresh_compatibility_check and revoke_compatibility_check mutations
statement: refresh_compatibility_check takes aReqId and bReqId, locates the min-side row, and replaces it via replaceLine returning NOT_FOUND when zero rows match and rejecting when two or more match; revoke_compatibility_check removes the row via replaceRange.
ac: refresh_compatibility_check locates the single min-side row and recomputes its self/peer pins via replaceLine.
refresh_compatibility_check returns NOT_FOUND when no matching row exists.
refresh_compatibility_check is rejected when two or more matching rows exist.
revoke_compatibility_check removes the compatibility row using a range replacement.
depends_on_titles: add_compatibility_check mutation with dedup frozen liveness guards and bidirectional pins

title: Compatibility cache validators W041 stale W042 missing W043 conflict-concealment with E012 relation template
statement: The validator emits SRS-W041 when a compatibility row's self or peer pin is stale against current semanticSha, SRS-W042 when a required compatibility row is missing for an adjacent pair, and SRS-W043 when a compatibility row conceals a conflict, and the SRS-E012 messageTemplate is extended with a relation placeholder.
ac: SRS-W041 is emitted when a stored self or peer pin differs from the endpoint's current semanticSha.
SRS-W042 is emitted when an expected compatibility row for an adjacent pair is absent.
SRS-W043 is emitted when a compatibility row conceals a detected conflict.
The SRS-E012 message renders the relation via a template placeholder.
W041, W042, and W043 do not collide with W044 or W045.
depends_on_titles: computeSemanticSha content-hash utility with fpv1 frozen vector
parseCompatibilityNotes strict tokenizer for compatibility Notes

title: list_dirty_edges read path with clean whitelist gate
statement: list_dirty_edges fresh-parses the workspace, builds an inverse index via summarizeTarget, and classifies each compatibility edge as clean only when all whitelist conditions hold (exactly one row, self pin equals current semanticSha, peer pin equals current, both endpoints cache-live, Notes parse, fpv match), otherwise dirty, additionally classifying orphaned and missing edges.
ac: An edge is reported clean only when row count is exactly 1 and both pins equal current semanticSha and both endpoints are cache-live and Notes parse and fpv matches.
Any edge failing one or more clean conditions is reported dirty with no blacklist path.
An edge whose endpoint is missing is classified missing and an edge whose peer was deleted is classified orphaned.
list_dirty_edges performs its own fresh parse rather than relying on summarizeTarget to parse.
depends_on_titles: computeSemanticSha content-hash utility with fpv1 frozen vector
parseCompatibilityNotes strict tokenizer for compatibility Notes

title: MCP registration of compatibility-check tools and edge read tools
statement: The MCP server registers add_compatibility_check, refresh_compatibility_check, and revoke_compatibility_check mutation tools and list_dirty_edges and list_compat_edges read tools with zod input schemas.
ac: The three compatibility mutation tools are registered with zod schemas.
list_dirty_edges and list_compat_edges are registered MCP read tools.
Each compatibility mutation tool forwards its inputs to the corresponding core mutation.
depends_on_titles: add_compatibility_check mutation with dedup frozen liveness guards and bidirectional pins
refresh_compatibility_check and revoke_compatibility_check mutations
list_dirty_edges read path with clean whitelist gate

title: update_requirement_statement mutation with new Requirement range helper
statement: update_requirement_statement replaces a requirement's statement body using a new range helper (since findSectionBodyRange cannot target the Requirement section) guarded against GFM table, code fence, and Acceptance Criteria boundary corruption.
ac: update_requirement_statement replaces the requirement statement text without altering the Acceptance Criteria section.
The mutation does not corrupt GFM tables or fenced code blocks adjacent to the statement.
A new range helper distinct from findSectionBodyRange locates the Requirement statement range.

title: edit_acceptance_criteria mutation
statement: edit_acceptance_criteria edits the text of acceptance criteria entries on a requirement block without altering their checked state or other sections.
ac: edit_acceptance_criteria updates the text of a targeted AC entry.
edit_acceptance_criteria leaves the checked/unchecked state of AC entries unchanged.
edit_acceptance_criteria does not modify the requirement statement or Trace Links sections.

title: MCP registration of gap mutation tools statement and AC edit
statement: The MCP server registers update_requirement_statement and edit_acceptance_criteria mutation tools with zod schemas that forward to their core mutations.
ac: update_requirement_statement is a registered MCP tool with a zod schema forwarding to the core mutation.
edit_acceptance_criteria is a registered MCP tool with a zod schema forwarding to the core mutation.
depends_on_titles: update_requirement_statement mutation with new Requirement range helper
edit_acceptance_criteria mutation

title: claim_step mutation with write-skew two-stage gate
statement: claim_step declares TouchesScope and TouchesReq and appends a state.md row, enforcing a two-stage gate where a direct same-REQ intersection is a HARD-BLOCK STEP_DIRECT_CONFLICT (force not allowed) and a transitive-only intersection is a SOFT-BLOCK STEP_OVERLAP (force pins overlaps), using computeBlastRadius for the closure and marking verified/frozen supersede targets STEP_SUPERSEDE_PROTECTED.
ac: claim_step appends a state.md row with the declared TouchesScope and TouchesReq.
A claim whose TouchesReq directly intersects an active step's TouchesReq is HARD-BLOCKed with STEP_DIRECT_CONFLICT and cannot be forced.
A claim that intersects only transitively via the closure is SOFT-BLOCKed with STEP_OVERLAP and force pins an overlaps marker.
A claim against a verified or frozen supersede target yields STEP_SUPERSEDE_PROTECTED.
When closure is unavailable the gate degrades to 1-hop direct hard-block with transitive treated as advisory.
depends_on_titles: state.md loader and parseStepState parser
compareReqId raw-byte ordering and computeBlastRadius closure utility

title: update_step_state mutation
statement: update_step_state updates an existing state.md step row's Status, DependsOn, and Updated fields.
ac: update_step_state changes the Status field of an existing step row to a value in active, merging, merged, abandoned.
update_step_state updates the DependsOn and Updated fields of the targeted step row.
update_step_state targeting a non-existent step returns NOT_FOUND.
depends_on_titles: state.md loader and parseStepState parser

title: list_steps topological ordering with cycle detection and advisories
statement: list_steps returns steps in Kahn topological order with cycle detection, emitting STEP_SUPERSEDE_PROTECTED, orphan, and drift advisories.
ac: list_steps returns steps in a valid topological order honoring DependsOn edges.
list_steps detects a dependency cycle and reports STEP_CYCLE rather than producing a partial order silently.
list_steps emits STEP_SUPERSEDE_PROTECTED, orphan, and drift advisories where applicable.
depends_on_titles: state.md loader and parseStepState parser

title: MCP registration of step state tools
statement: The MCP server registers claim_step, update_step_state, and list_steps tools with zod schemas that forward to their core implementations.
ac: claim_step, update_step_state, and list_steps are registered MCP tools with zod schemas.
Each step-state tool forwards its inputs to the corresponding core implementation.
depends_on_titles: claim_step mutation with write-skew two-stage gate
update_step_state mutation
list_steps topological ordering with cycle detection and advisories

title: kiwi-step lightweight step-local authoring skill
statement: The kiwi-step skill provides lightweight step-local requirement authoring against docs/spec/steps/<name>/ using claim_step, the step-scoped mutations, and step-local validation.
ac: kiwi-step claims a step via claim_step before authoring step-local requirements.
kiwi-step authors requirements only under docs/spec/steps/<name>/ and never directly in body scope files.
kiwi-step runs step-local validation via validate_step as part of its workflow.
depends_on_titles: claim_step mutation with write-skew two-stage gate
speckiwi step validate command

title: supersede_requirement strict two-call mutation with guards and A1 invalidation
statement: supersede_requirement performs the strict ordered two-call sequence T1 add_requirement (id unspecified, trace supersedes oldId) capturing newId then T2 hardened updateStatus(oldId, discarded), enforcing self-reference, reverse-duplicate, and N>1 ambiguity guards, ensuring idempotent journal resumption by omitting reason or pre-checking the Change Note, and invalidating the oldId endpoint via revoke_compatibility_check.
ac: supersede_requirement executes T1 add_requirement then T2 hardened updateStatus in that fixed order, capturing the newId from T1.
supersede_requirement is rejected on self-reference, on a reverse-direction duplicate, and when N>1 successors are ambiguous.
The hardened updateStatus discard in T2 honors the verified-regression exit guard.
Journal resumption is idempotent: re-running does not append a duplicate Change Notes row.
The oldId endpoint's compatibility rows are invalidated via revoke_compatibility_check after supersede.
depends_on_titles: updateStatus verified-regression exit guard with explicit override
refresh_compatibility_check and revoke_compatibility_check mutations

title: promote_step_requirement mutation with reservation uniqueness verbatim insert
statement: promote_step_requirement with id, fromStep, toScope inserts a step's pre-minted canonical requirement id verbatim into the target body scope after verifying global uniqueness against a reservation view (HEAD plus step plus reserved), preserving the step's id rather than auto-generating one.
ac: promote_step_requirement inserts the step requirement into toScope using the step's existing id verbatim.
promote_step_requirement rejects the insert when the id already exists in the reservation view.
promote_step_requirement does not auto-generate or alter the requirement id.
depends_on_titles: Workspace parser origin split into body and step records

title: MultiFileCommit four-phase engine with durable merge-journal crash recovery
statement: MultiFileCommit (Option A, net-new merge only) commits a single-REQ change touching a step file and a body file in one atomic operation via four phases (render all, stale-check, write tmp, batch rename) backed by a durable merge-journal (renames, sha256, backup) so an interrupted merge is rolled forward or back by the next merge, reusing the export-promoted assertFreshSnapshot.
ac: MultiFileCommit renders all files, performs a stale-check, writes tmp files, then performs all renames as the final phase.
A durable merge-journal records renames, sha256 hashes, and backups before the rename phase.
An interrupted merge is detected as half-applied by the next merge and rolled forward or back.
The journal write is itself atomic via tmp-rename, re-entrant resumption is idempotent, and a partial stale condition aborts all-or-nothing.
state.md is not included in the commit plan.

title: merge-journal append-log with resume skip
statement: The merge-journal records renames, sha256 hashes, and the captured requirement id as durable append-log entries that a resuming merge reads to skip already-applied operations.
ac: Each merge-journal entry records the renames, their sha256 hashes, and the captured requirement id.
A resuming merge reads the journal and skips operations already recorded as applied.
Journal entries are appended durably before the corresponding rename is performed.
depends_on_titles: MultiFileCommit four-phase engine with durable merge-journal crash recovery

title: MCP registration of supersede and promote mutation tools
statement: The MCP server registers supersede_requirement and promote_step_requirement mutation tools with zod schemas that forward to their core implementations.
ac: supersede_requirement is a registered MCP tool with a zod schema forwarding to the core mutation.
promote_step_requirement is a registered MCP tool with a zod schema forwarding to the core mutation.
depends_on_titles: supersede_requirement strict two-call mutation with guards and A1 invalidation
promote_step_requirement mutation with reservation uniqueness verbatim insert

title: diff_steps four-way classification keyed on semanticSha
statement: diff_steps classifies each step-vs-body requirement difference into NEW, UPDATE, CONFLICT-PARTIAL, or CONFLICT-FULL-GUARDED using computeSemanticSha as the comparison key with later-step-wins precedence for draft/evolving peers.
ac: diff_steps uses computeSemanticSha as the equality key when comparing step and body requirements.
diff_steps classifies a step-only id as NEW and a changed-body id as UPDATE.
diff_steps classifies conflicting changes as CONFLICT-PARTIAL or CONFLICT-FULL-GUARDED.
For draft/evolving same-rank peers the later step takes precedence.
depends_on_titles: computeSemanticSha content-hash utility with fpv1 frozen vector
list_dirty_edges read path with clean whitelist gate

title: MCP registration of diff_steps read tool
statement: The MCP server registers a diff_steps read tool with a zod schema that returns the four-way classification of step-vs-body requirement differences.
ac: diff_steps is a registered MCP read tool with a zod schema.
diff_steps returns NEW, UPDATE, CONFLICT-PARTIAL, and CONFLICT-FULL-GUARDED classifications to the caller.
depends_on_titles: diff_steps four-way classification keyed on semanticSha

title: kiwi-spec-merge per-REQ sequential merge orchestrator skill
statement: The kiwi-spec-merge skill orchestrates a merge as a sequence of per-REQ single-REQ req-scoped calls (dry-run, user approval, 1-REQ call, journal, resume), routing each diff_steps class to promote_step_requirement (NEW), in-place body updates (UPDATE), or supersede_requirement (CONFLICT), with evidence migration and a post-merge verification-decrease report, never invoking an N-REQ batch finalize tool.
ac: kiwi-spec-merge issues exactly one REQ per mutation call and never calls an N-REQ batch finalize tool.
kiwi-spec-merge runs a dry-run and obtains user approval before each applied per-REQ call.
kiwi-spec-merge routes NEW to promote_step_requirement, UPDATE to in-place body updates, and CONFLICT to supersede_requirement.
kiwi-spec-merge resumes an interrupted merge from the merge-journal without duplicating applied calls.
kiwi-spec-merge produces a post-merge verification-decrease report and handles loser-evidence migration.
depends_on_titles: diff_steps four-way classification keyed on semanticSha
supersede_requirement strict two-call mutation with guards and A1 invalidation
promote_step_requirement mutation with reservation uniqueness verbatim insert
MultiFileCommit four-phase engine with durable merge-journal crash recovery
